title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This represents a failure of the autonomous system to detect and avoid a slow-moving object in its path, despite having both sensor systems and a human monitor in the vehicle.

The incident occurred during normal deployment on public streets in a residential neighborhood. It would have required either the vehicle's perception system to reliably identify the duck as an obstacle before collision, or the safety operator to intervene and brake. Whether the system failed to detect the duck, failed to classify it as an obstacle, or failed to brake in response is not established by the available reports.

Following the incident, Avride disputed a separate claim about the vehicle failing to stop at a stop sign, though the core issue of the collision itself was not contested. The company has since restricted the vehicle's operating area and begun simulation testing to improve performance.

summary:
# Summary

An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, did not stop after hitting the duck that was nesting outside a local Italian restaurant. A resident posted about the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group, claiming the vehicle did not slow down and also failed to stop at a stop sign. The duck's eggs have since been collected by local residents and placed in an incubator.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and reviewed vehicle data multiple times. The company disputed the claim about the stop sign, stating the vehicle made complete and appropriate stops. In response, Avride has excluded certain streets around the lake from its testing operations and is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo and Tesla, also operate in Austin.
